mechanisms.name: QoS classes and per-request deadline derivation
mechanisms.description: Defines two QoS classes (interactive, non-interactive) with application-specified SLO targets. Interactive requests get a TTFT deadline D_first = t_arrival + SLO_TTFT and per-token deadlines D_n = t_arrival + SLO_TTFT + (n-1)*SLO_TBT; non-interactive requests get a single completion deadline D_total = t_arrival + SLO_TTLT. These deadlines are the input to all later scheduling decisions.

evidence.quote: QoServe defines two QoS classes: interactive and non interactive.
D_n =t_arrival+SLO_TTFT +(n− 1)· SLO_TBT

mechanisms.boundary: Only defines deadlines; does not itself schedule. TBT deadlines are maintained by dynamic chunking, not by the priority function.
mechanisms.merge_reason: 两个候选描述的是同一件事：把 QoS 类别映射为每请求的截止时间（TTFT/TBT/TTLT 公式）。A01 与 B02 的公式、页面和边界完全一致，只是措辞不同，因此合并为同一机制，而不是两个独立机制。

mechanisms.name: Dynamic chunking (slack-driven chunk size maximization)
mechanisms.description: Instead of a fixed chunk size sized for the strictest QoS class, QoServe computes per-decode-request slack (next-token deadline minus current time) and uses the accumulated slack plus decode-batch characteristics to pick the largest prefill chunk that still meets all latency budgets, opportunistically raising throughput when slack exists and shrinking when an interactive request is decoding.

evidence.quote: QoServe employs dynamic chunking to opportunistically maximize the chunk size for the prefill request by exploiting any slack in the deadlines of the requests being currently serviced.
we define slack as the difference between the deadline for the next token (Eq. 2) and current time
we exploit this slack by dynamically increasing the chunk size, adding more prefill tokens from requests B and D

mechanisms.boundary: Sets the per-iteration prefill token budget C; does not decide which request fills it. Gains are limited under PD disaggregation where a large fixed chunk (8K) is used.
mechanisms.merge_reason: A02 与 B03 都描述同一个基于 slack 的动态分块策略：用解码请求的 slack 决定 prefill chunk 大小。两者共享同一公式、同一目的（在延迟预算内最大化吞吐），只是 B03 多列了示例页，因此合并。

mechanisms.name: Random-forest batch latency predictor
mechanisms.description: A lightweight random-forest model predicts execution time of a candidate batch from batch statistics (number of requests, context lengths, chunk size) and is used to select the chunk size maximizing throughput within the latency budget. Trained on MLP/attention latency profiles gathered via the Vidur simulator harness; tuned to under-predict chunk size to avoid latency overshoot. Runs on CPU with <10% error margin.

evidence.quote: we train a lightweight random forest model which predicts the execution time of a given batch
We tune the model to err on the side of under-predicting chunk size.

mechanisms.boundary: Provides the latency estimate used to pick chunk size; does not rank requests.
mechanisms.merge_reason: A03 与 B04 是同一个随机森林延迟预测器：输入批次统计、输出执行时间、用于选择 chunk 大小，且都提到 Vidur 采集训练数据与故意低估。描述完全重合，故合并。

mechanisms.name: Hybrid prioritization (EDF–SRPF interpolation)
mechanisms.description: Computes a per-request priority as a linear combination of the deadline term (EDF semantics) and estimated remaining work (SRPF semantics): P_i = t_arrival + SLO_TTFT + α*Prefill_rem for interactive, and P_i = t_arrival + SLO_TTLT + α*(Prefill_rem + Decode_rem) for non-interactive. α is a tunable interpolation factor giving EDF behavior at low load and SRPF-like behavior under overload.

evidence.quote: QoServe smoothly interpolates between EDF and SRPF to compute the priority of a request.

mechanisms.name: Violation checker and eager relegation
mechanisms.description: Before admitting a prefill request, the violation checker validates it has not violated and will not violate its QoS targets in the current iteration; if so it is moved to the relegated queue and another request is chosen. Relegated requests are served opportunistically at low load (eventual completion, not permanent rejection). In multi-tenant settings, application hints (free vs paid tier) preferentially relegate low-priority requests; high-priority requests are relegated only after low-priority ones are exhausted.

evidence.quote: The violation checker module validates that the chosen request has not already violated (or will not violate) its QoS targets in the current iteration.
if a request has already violated its TTFT / TTLT deadline, or is about to violate it in the current iteration, then QoServe de-prioritizes this request into a relegated queue
The relegated requests are serviced opportunistically during periods of lower system load, ensuring eventual completion without permanent rejection

mechanisms.boundary: Degrades service for a subset; relegated requests are not permanently rejected and are served opportunistically. Triggered by the violation checker; does not preempt decode requests. Relies on application-provided priority hints for tier ordering.
mechanisms.merge_reason: A06 与 B08 都描述“违规检查器 + 主动降级”这一组合：检查是否已/将违反截止时间，若违反则移入 relegated 队列，并利用应用提示优先降级低优先级请求。两者引用同一段原文，边界一致，故合并。

mechanisms.name: Selective preemption
mechanisms.description: A prefill request may be preempted for a higher-priority request only if (1) it is in the prefill queue (decode requests are never preempted) and (2) preempting it for one iteration does not cause a deadline violation. This avoids head-of-line blocking while limiting KV-cache memory pressure.

mechanisms.description: Requests live in a prefill queue, decode queue, or relegated queue. Completed prefills move to the decode queue.

1: # Sarathi-Serve: Deadline-aware Scheduling
2: 
3: This is a specialized branch of Sarathi-Serve that implements deadline-aware scheduling for LLM inference.
4: 
5: ### Environment Setup
6: 
7: Create a Python 3.10 environment:
8: 
9: ```sh
10: # Create the environment named 'niyama'
11: conda create -n niyama python=3.10 -y
12: 
13: # Activate the environment
14: conda activate niyama
15: ```
16: 
17: ### Install Sarathi-Serve
18: 
19: ```sh
20: pip install -e . https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/download/v0.1.1/flashinfer-0.1.1+cu121torch2.3-cp310-cp310-linux_x86_64.whl
21: ```
22: 
23: ### Model Access & Environment Variables
24: 
25: To run the benchmarks, you must have access to the models (e.g., Llama-3-8B, Qwen-2.5) on Hugging Face. You must also export your Hugging Face token:
26: 
27: ```sh
28: export HF_TOKEN="your_huggingface_token_here"
29: ```
30: 
31: ### Dataset Preparation
32: 
33: Before running benchmarks, download the required Azure trace datasets into the `data/processed_traces` directory:
34: 
35: ```sh
36: mkdir -p data/processed_traces
37: 
38: # Download Code traces
39: wget -O data/processed_traces/AzureLLMInferenceTrace_code_1week.csv https://azurepublicdatasettraces.blob.core.windows.net/azurellminfererencetrace/AzureLLMInferenceTrace_code_1week.csv
40: 
41: # Download Conversation traces
42: wget -O data/processed_traces/AzureLLMInferenceTrace_conv_1week.csv https://azurepublicdatasettraces.blob.core.windows.net/azurellminfererencetrace/AzureLLMInferenceTrace_conv_1week.csv
43: ```
44: 
45: ### Reproducibility
46: 
47: To ensure accurate measurement of CUDA kernel elapsed times and guarantee reproducibility of numbers, please follow these configuration steps before running benchmarks:
48: 
49: 1.  **Reset GPU Configurations**
50:     Reset all GPUs to their default configurations to clear any previous states.
51:     ```sh
52:     nvidia-smi --gpu-reset
53:     ```
54: 
55: 2.  **Enable Persistence Mode**
56:     Enable persistence mode to keep the target GPU initialized even when no clients are connected.
57:     ```sh
58:     # Replace <gpu_id> with your specific GPU ID (e.g., 3)
59:     nvidia-smi -pm ENABLED -i <gpu_id>
60:     ```
61: 
62: 3.  **Lock GPU Clocks**
63:     Lock the GPU clocks to their Thermal Design Power (TDP) frequency to ensure uniform numbers across runs.
64:     ```sh
65:     # Lock GPU clocks to TDP
66:     nvidia-smi --lock-gpu-clocks=tdp,tdp
67:     
68:     # Alternatively, set the application clock to the base TDP frequency (e.g., 1065 MHz on A100)
69:     nvidia-smi ac 1512,1065 -i <gpu_id>
70:     nvidia-smi -lgc tdp,tdp -i <gpu_id>
71:     ```
72: 
73: 4.  **Code-Level Determinism**
74:     * **Set Random Seeds**: Empirically, numbers may vary across runs. To mitigate this, set the seed value for both standard and CUDA random number generators:
75:         ```python
76:         torch.manual_seed(random_seed)
77:         torch.cuda.manual_seed(random_seed)
78:         ```
79:     * **Kernel Isolation**: Avoid running different kernels for the sake of measurement inside a single process, as this causes variance in numbers.
80: 
81: ### Running Experiments
82: 
83: * Run `tester.sh` to do a test run.
84: * Run `fig10_11.sh` to recreate Figure 10 and 11 from the paper.

93: This branch of Sarathi-Serve implements deadline-based scheduling approach. The branch leverages chunking concepts (for more information about chunking, see [Sarathi paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.16369)). Key features include:
94: 
95: 1. **SLA-aware Scheduler**: Maximizes deadline-slack and improves serving throughput by making scheduling decisions based on SLA constraints.
96: 
97: 2. **Key Features**:
98:    - Deadline-aware ordering of requests
99:    - Strategic request selection under high loads to maintain throughput
100:    - Dynamic prefill chunk size selection to balance throughput and latency guarantees
101:    - Tunable parameters to adjust priority based on request length and arrival time
102: 
103: 3. **Implementation Details**:
104:    ### Scheduling Logic
105:    - The main scheduling loop is implemented in **`sarathi/core/scheduler/deadline_scheduler.py`**:
106:    - **Lines 271–277**: Invoke the **chunk size predictor** to determine how many tokens to schedule.
107:    - **Lines 54–167**: Contain the implementation of the chunk size predictor itself.
108:    - **Line 300**: Performs **eager relegation**, where requests that are predicted to miss their deadline are deprioritized.
109: 
110:    ### Request Metadata and Prioritization
111:    Defined in **`sarathi/core/datatypes/sequence.py`**:
112:    - **Line 11**: Defines `TIER_DEADLINES`, the SLA tiers that requests may fall into.
113:    - **Lines 70–75**: Randomly assign each request to an SLA tier.
114:    - **Line 79**: Defines the **hybrid prioritization constant**.
115:    - **Lines 88–109**: Contain the **sequence comparator**, which orders requests based on the hybrid prioritization mechanism.
116:    - **Lines 106–107** (not commented out anymore): Control the weight between arrival time and remaining tokens (the latter acting as a proxy for remaining processing time).
117:    - **TTLT (Time-To-Last-Token) SLA**:  
118:    - Output length is predicted using `num_dec_tokens`.  
119:    - Approximate **Time-To-First-Token (TTFT)** is estimated by subtracting `num_dec_tokens × TBT_SLA` seconds from the SLA (assuming each decode token takes TBT_SLA seconds).

121:    ### Chunk Size Prediction
122:    - Implemented in **`chunk_size_predictor/predictor.py`**.
123:    - This module is responsible for **fitting the linear regression model** on data collected from previous runs.
124:    - The trained model is written inside the **deadline scheduler**, which uses it to predict processing times and decide chunk sizes when scheduling requests.

58:     def _predict_batch_time(self, batch_decode_context, batch_prefill_context,

60:         """
61:         Predict execution time using two stratified linear models:
62:         - tokens_0_512:      0 < total_tokens <= 512
63:         - tokens_513_plus:   total_tokens > 512
64:         """
65:         # Total tokens
66:         batch_num_tokens = batch_num_prefill_tokens + batch_num_decode_tokens
67: 
68:         # Stratified models from latest training logs, memory_bound v/s compute_bound regime
69:         tokens_0_512 = {
70:             "coefficients": {
71:                 "batch_num_tokens":      5.882475e-05,
72:                 "batch_num_prefill_tokens": 2.247956e-05,
73:                 "batch_num_decode_tokens":  3.634519e-05,
74:                 "batch_decode_context":   1.111258e-07,
75:                 "batch_prefill_context":  7.554773e-07,
76:             },
77:             "intercept": 0.014936,
78:         }
79: 
80:         tokens_513_plus = {
81:             "coefficients": {
82:                 "batch_num_tokens":      2.719050e-05,
83:                 "batch_num_prefill_tokens": 6.863043e-05,
84:                 "batch_num_decode_tokens": -4.143993e-05,
85:                 "batch_decode_context":   1.663409e-07,
86:                 "batch_prefill_context":  2.727223e-06,
87:             },
88:             "intercept": 0.005004,
89:         }
90: 
91:         # Select bin (ensure 513 maps to the 513+ model)
92:         model = tokens_0_512 if (batch_num_tokens <= 512) else tokens_513_plus
93: 
94:         # Linear prediction
95:         c = model["coefficients"]
96:         y = model["intercept"]
97:         y += c["batch_num_tokens"]        * batch_num_tokens
98:         y += c["batch_num_prefill_tokens"]* batch_num_prefill_tokens
99:         y += c["batch_num_decode_tokens"] * batch_num_decode_tokens
100:         y += c["batch_decode_context"]    * batch_decode_context
101:         y += c["batch_prefill_context"]   * batch_prefill_context
102: 
103:         return y

106:     def _get_prefill_size_by_slack(self, min_slack, batch_decode_context, batch_prefill_context, batch_num_decode_tokens):
107:         """Find max prefill tokens that can be processed within min_slack time.
108:         Search based on total tokens (prefill + decode) but return prefill tokens,
109:         while respecting memory budget constraints."""
110:         # Token Search Space from 128 to 8192 in steps of 128
111:         token_search_space = TOKEN_SEARCH_SPACE
112:         
113:         # Get memory budget information
114:         free_blocks = self.block_manager.gpu_allocator.get_num_free_blocks()
115:         block_size = self.block_manager.block_size
116: 
117:         # We say that the memory budget is the total number of tokens whose kv cache can be stored divided by 32
118:         # This way if we can ensure that next few batches have sufficient memory budget, we can avoid OOM errors
119:         memory_budget = (free_blocks * block_size) // 32
120:         if memory_budget < 1000:

121:             # Under memory constrained conditions, range goes from 128 to 512
122:             token_search_space = LOW_MEMORY_TOKEN_SEARCH_SPACE
123:         
124:         # Binary search through the predefined token space
125:         best_total_tokens = token_search_space[0]
126:         best_total_tokens_pred_time = self._predict_batch_time(
127:             batch_decode_context, batch_prefill_context,
128:             max(0, best_total_tokens - batch_num_decode_tokens), batch_num_decode_tokens
129:         )
130:         if min_slack <= 0:
131:             return max(0, best_total_tokens - batch_num_decode_tokens), best_total_tokens_pred_time
132: 
133:         lo, hi = 0, len(token_search_space) - 1
134:         while lo <= hi:
135:             mid = (lo + hi) // 2
136:             total_tokens = token_search_space[mid]
137:             prefill_tokens = max(0, total_tokens - batch_num_decode_tokens)
138: 
139:             predicted_time = self._predict_batch_time(
140:                 batch_decode_context, batch_prefill_context,
141:                 prefill_tokens, batch_num_decode_tokens
142:             )
143: 
144:             # Adjust predicted time based on pred_thres
145:             adjusted_predicted_time = predicted_time * self.pred_thres
146:             if adjusted_predicted_time <= min_slack:
147:                 # feasible -> record and try to push higher (more tokens within slack)
148:                 best_total_tokens = total_tokens
149:                 best_total_tokens_pred_time = predicted_time
150:                 lo = mid + 1
151:             else:
152:                 # infeasible -> need fewer total tokens
153:                 hi = mid - 1
154:          # -------------------- Buffered logging --------------------
155:         enable_logging = False
156:         if enable_logging:

158:                 self._log_dc_buffer = []
159:             log_line = f'{batch_decode_context},{batch_prefill_context},' \
160:                     f'{batch_num_decode_tokens},{min_slack},' \
161:                     f'{best_total_tokens},{best_total_tokens_pred_time}\n'

55: def train_stratified_models(df: pd.DataFrame, min_samples_per_bin: int = 100):
56:     df_filtered = df[df["batch_execution_time"] <= 1.0].copy()
57:     print(

60:     )

62:     models = {}
63:     for low, high, name in TOKEN_RANGES:
64:         if high == float("inf"):
65:             rng_df = df_filtered[df_filtered["batch_num_tokens"] > low]
66:             print(f"Training model for batch_num_tokens > {low}")
67:         else:
68:             rng_df = df_filtered[
69:                 (df_filtered["batch_num_tokens"] > low)
70:                 & (df_filtered["batch_num_tokens"] <= high)

72:             print(f"Training model for {low} < batch_num_tokens <= {high}")

76:             print(f"Warning: Too few samples in range {low}-{high}, skipping bin '{name}'")
77:             continue

80:         y = rng_df["batch_execution_time"]
81: 
82:         X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(

85:

104:         models[name] = {

119: def predict_with_models(df: pd.DataFrame, models: Dict[str, dict]) -> pd.DataFrame:
120:     df = df.copy()

121:     mask_valid = df["batch_execution_time"] <= 1.0
122: 
123:     df.loc[mask_valid, "model_used"] = None
124:     df.loc[mask_valid, "predicted_time"] = np.nan
125: 
126:     for name, info in models.items():
127:         low, high = info["low"], info["high"]
128:         if high == float("inf"):
129:             mask_bin = mask_valid & (df["batch_num_tokens"] > low)
130:         else:
131:             mask_bin = mask_valid & (df["batch_num_tokens"] > low) & (df["batch_num_tokens"] <= high)
132: 
133:         rows = int(mask_bin.sum())
134:         if rows > 0:
135:             X = df.loc[mask_bin, FEATURES]
136:             preds = info["model"].predict(X)
137:             df.loc[mask_bin, "predicted_time"] = preds
138:             df.loc[mask_bin, "model_used"] = name
139: 
140:     # Fallback for unmatched valid rows
141:     missing = mask_valid & df["predicted_time"].isna()
142:     if missing.any():
143:         first_model_name = next(iter(models.keys()))
144:         print(f"Fallback: applying '{first_model_name}' to {int(missing.sum())} unmatched rows")
145:         X = df.loc[missing, FEATURES]
146:         preds = models[first_model_name]["model"].predict(X)
147:         df.loc[missing, "predicted_time"] = preds
148:         df.loc[missing, "model_used"] = f"{first_model_name}_fallback"
149: 
150:     return df
